analysis: Both changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/hardware-support.md, docs/architecture/inference.md): date bumps, a new 'Calibration ownership and foreground admission' section (head lines 335-367), a new 'Model startup calibration' section in inference.md, and code-map rows. No source, key, attestation, protocol, or authorization behavior is changed by the diff. The docs describe provider-local calibration only. They say it uses existing KV and service budgets, does not lower activation or OS reserves, does not raise concurrency, and leaves the wire fields and the platform memory contract unchanged. Claimed controls: a single calibration session per Mac; foreground customer requests cancel calibration and wait for actual retirement while original deadlines and memory admission stay authoritative; startupWarmup is excluded from rate learning; calibration produces no served-request or output-token counters; staged observations are discarded on a cancelled or non-nominal cell. Security-relevant points for later passes if code lands: calibration observations feed capacity heartbeats and routing evidence (platform-owned), so rate inflation or poisoning by a provider (ADV-001) is already in the provider's control and is not newly enabled by the docs. Calibration uses synthetic probes, so no consumer prompts (A-001) or prefix-cache entries (T-041) are involved; the docs state probes are uncached. The T-010 cancellation and GPU-availability analogue is that foreground cancellation waits on retirement bounded by existing deadlines. No threat-model entries are invalidated. I did not verify that the documented code paths exist, since the source changes are not in this batch; unchanged callers were not examined.
